title: Redwood migration demo - OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood
next_steps: Send parity mapping spreadsheet + API samples
Intro to Solutions Engineering for Dedicated sizing
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked BrightTask through a migration demo mapping common OpenAI/Anthropic/Together API calls to Redwood endpoints. Discussed model parity, streaming and function call mapping, auth and SSO, VPC/KMS options, Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, and next steps to run a short POC benchmark. Customer is interested in cost/latency comparison and security compliance artifacts.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted protection and VPC
Security: SOC2, KMS, RBAC, audit logs
transcript:
00:00 Karen Liu: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Karen from Redwood, i have Miguel and Jin with me on the technical side, can you hear us ok?
00:06 Aisha Patel: yep we're good, thanks, excited to see the migration flow, we've been evaluating moving some of our OpenAI/Together workloads to Redwood.
00:15 Miguel Santos: great, quick agenda — we'll demo API parity mapping, show console, discuss Optimize suggestions and finishing with a POC plan. We'll try to call out where requests differ from OpenAI/Anthropic.
00:27 Tom Reynolds: quick heads up, our main concerns are latency for chat, cost per 1M tokens, and data residency since some requests contain customer PII.
00:36 Miguel Santos: understood, we'll touch on VPC/private deployment and KMS a bit later, also how Dedicated can help with throughput guarantees.
00:44 Jin Park: okay diving in — first a parity overview. On the left you'd have your usual OpenAI/Anthropic endpoints: /v1/chat/completions, streaming with chunked events, function calls etc. On Redwood we expose a unified /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoint plus a streaming SSE and websocket option. For most SDKs it's a thin replace — API key, content-type, and a few param names map directly.
01:10 Miguel Santos: example, OpenAI's model "gpt-4o" maps to our "redwood-4o" naming but we also expose compatibility aliases so you can keep the same literal model name in many cases. For Anthropic assistant-style you can map role/content to the chat messages field.
01:26 Aisha Patel: interesting, do you preserve function call semantics? We rely heavily on function-calling.
01:32 Miguel Santos: yes, function calling is supported. Slight nuance: we return a structured "tool_invocation" event in streaming mode, and the console shows the parsed args. In practice the SDKs currently accept the same functions array and the response shape is similar, though some keys differ (e.g., "name" vs "tool_name" in the raw transcript for older SDKs).
01:55 Markus Chen: small note, do you support incremental KV cache warmups? our latency suffers on cold starts.
02:01 Jin Park: we do—redwood runtime supports prefix caching and KV cache reuse across requests within the same session id. That cuts repeated prompt tokens substantially. On Dedicated you can also pin model variants with warmed-up cache.
02:14 Tom Reynolds: okay, what about embeddings — we use Together embeddings for semantic search. How do they compare and what's the mapping?
02:21 Miguel Santos: embeddings map to /v1/embeddings; models have one-to-one equivalents, e.g. together-sim -> redwood-sim. For quality we provide evaluation reports; we can run a sample set and give cosine similarity deltas. Also Optimize suggests quantization profiles if you want lower cost at slight quality tradeoff.
02:44 Aisha Patel: can you show the console? we want to see how routing and fallback rules look.
02:48 Jin Park: switching to the console — sharing screen — you can see routes mapped by API key, region, and model families. Here's a policy: prefer redwood-4o-hosted for web tier, fallback to redwood-4o-dedicated if latency spikes, and last resort to a cheaper quantized variant. You can set percentage rollouts for canaries.
03:13 Nina Gomez: does the console show token-level cost? that's huge for finance.
03:17 Miguel Santos: yes, per-token cost breakdown per route and model. Also trace view shows which requests triggered batching or cache hits.
03:25 Aisha Patel: security — does Redwood support customer-managed KMS or HSM? we need non-default key control.
03:31 Karen Liu: yes, for Private deployments and Dedicated with certain enterprise plans we support KMS integrations and HSM options. You also get audit logs, RBAC, and SAML SSO. We'll share SOC2 and ISO artifacts after the call.
03:43 Lena Park: and data retention controls? we can't have logs persisted for more than 30 days in prod.
03:48 Miguel Santos: you can configure retention per route and we have a purge API. In Private deployments you can disable transcript logging entirely.
03:56 Aisha Patel: about migration pain — what are typical code diffs? i.e. tokenization differences or prompt tweaks required?
04:03 Jin Park: tokenization can differ slightly; we recommend a small prompt audit. Most customers do a find-and-replace for API endpoints, keep their prompts, and run a 1k sample check. We'll provide a parity spreadsheet with recommended prompt adjustments and example SDK calls.
04:19 Tom Reynolds: any pitfalls with rate limits when moving from OpenAI? we have bursty traffic.
04:25 Miguel Santos: Redwood offers flexible rate limits and dedicated throughput on Dedicated. For hosted plans we have configurable burst windows and auto-throttling. We can also put a rate limiter in front of certain routes via the console and allow bursting to Dedicated pools.
04:39 Markus Chen: let's talk about benchmarks — we need a POC to compare p95 latency for chat at 2k context and cost per 100k tokens.
04:47 Karen Liu: that's doable; typically we run a 1–2 week POC with sample traffic. For benchmarks we instrument end-to-end including your client side. We'll provide a test harness and collect latency/cost and model output diffs.
04:59 Aisha Patel: good. are there changes needed for streaming in our frontend? we use eventsource for OpenAI.
05:06 Jin Park: same pattern should work; we've got SSE examples that are nearly identical. A small header change and parsing for the "tool_invocation" event in streaming. We'll also share a react example for websockets.
05:20 Nina Gomez: does Redwood support multi-model routing? we sometimes route to different models for short vs long form.
05:26 Miguel Santos: yes, you can configure routing rules by prompt heuristics, user tier, or latency targets. The optimize module can auto-suggest when to route to cheaper quantized variants.
05:36 Tom Reynolds: curious about unit economics — if we quantize to 4-bit, what's the expected quality hit?
05:42 Miguel Santos: depends on model and task. For embeddings it's often negligible; for instruction-following chat there's sometimes a small delta. We'll run your eval set and include an automated quality regression alert in the POC.
05:56 Aisha Patel: any gotchas with Anthropic style completions — they have a different safety layer.
06:02 Miguel Santos: Redwood has content-safety hooks and policy layers; you can enable Anthropic-like safety filters but sometimes prompt engineering changes are required. We surface safety events in console and provide filtering options.
06:12 Lena Park: compliance question—does Redwood provide a contract addendum for data processing and EU data residency?
06:18 Karen Liu: yes, we have DPA addendum options and region-specific hosting. We'll include the legal contact and typical SLA language.
06:25 Tom Reynolds: ok let's role-play a migration path. Phase 1: parity mapping + smoke tests. Phase 2: small POC with 100 rps for 3 days. Phase 3: roll to prod with canary.
06:36 Karen Liu: that matches what we recommend. We'll scope Dedicated sizing after the POC if you need throughput guarantees.
06:42 Markus Chen: cost model — do you offer committed discounts for Dedicated?
06:45 Karen Liu: yes, committed monthly/annual contracts for Dedicated with discount tiers. We can put sample numbers in the pricing sheet.
06:52 Nina Gomez: can you show a short code example switching from OpenAI to Redwood for function calls?
06:56 Miguel Santos: sure — here's a quick snippet: replace openai endpoint with api.redwood.ai/v1/chat, pass same messages array, functions array is accepted; minor rename on response payload we show in console docs. I'll paste the example in the slack thread after this call.
07:13 Aisha Patel: i'm worried about subtle token differences affecting hallucination rates. how do you measure that?
07:19 Jin Park: we use prompt-specific evals and compare model outputs with reference answers. For hallucination we run precision/recall style metrics and report diffs. Optimize can then suggest prompt or model variants.
07:32 Tom Reynolds: about observability — do you capture bad requests or overruns? we need tracing.
07:37 Miguel Santos: yes, traces include request payloads (if enabled), latency breakdown, and per-token breakdown. You can export traces to your existing tracing stack.
07:46 Karen Liu: okay we'll recap. Next steps: we'll send the parity mapping sheet and API snippets, share SOC2/security docs, and set up the POC benchmark. Any other asks?
07:57 Aisha Patel: please include the quantization impact report and an estimated cost for 100k tokens/day.
08:03 Karen Liu: noted. we'll follow up with an email and attach the sample harness.
08:07 Tom Reynolds: timeline — can we start POC week of 7/28?
08:10 Karen Liu: yes we'll propose slots, and Miguel will follow up on the harness.
08:14 Miguel Santos: thanks everyone — after the call i'll drop links: parity spreadsheet, code samples, SOC2 doc, and a bench harness repo.
08:22 Karen Liu: thanks all, bye.
08:23 Aisha Patel: thanks, bye.
